questions.stem: What does the width of an arrow in a Sankey diagram represent?

options.text: The speed of the energy transfer
The amount of energy being transferred

questions.explanation: In a Sankey diagram, the width of each arrow is proportional to the amount of energy being transferred. Wider arrows represent more energy. The useful output is shown going straight across while wasted energy branches off.

questions.stem: When energy is 'dissipated', what typically happens to it?

options.text: It is converted into nuclear energy
It spreads out as thermal energy into the surroundings
It returns to its original store

questions.explanation: When energy is dissipated, it spreads out into the surroundings as thermal energy and becomes less useful. The energy is not destroyed — it still exists but is very difficult to recover and use again.
